estimate_basis_note: the row estimates assume a database whose optimizer statistics are up to date (ANALYZE TABLE was run after the data was built); on a database with stale or missing statistics the plans, and so the estimates, can differ; they also assume that the database the statements were captured on and the database the estimate is used on are in the same maintenance state: the rebuild and aggregate processes of the application (for BookStack, regenerate-references) were run on both or on neither, and then ANALYZE TABLE was run on both, because a table such a process rewrites can hold different rows in another state

width.reason: the range of the two-coefficient fits made by leaving each of the 7 calibration scenarios out

calibration_range.reason: the range of the two-coefficient fits made by leaving each of the 7 calibration scenarios out

app_limit_risk_memory.rule: marked when measured_over_predicted x the predicted peak memory of one request (section 6.2) >= limit_bytes; whether the formula held within +-30% in the extrapolation tests does not switch the mark off

app_limit_risk_placeholders.rule: marked when the largest number of values one statement of the route carries at the scenario's table size (fixed + what a list holds x table size / the scale of the capture) > limit_values
app_limit_risk_placeholders.limit_rps_note: the limit rps counts the marked routes as requests that run to the end; a marked route may be cut by the app's limit first

allocation.rule: a route marked by the placeholder side or the memory side at the scenario's table size is taken out of the mix; the rps of the routes of its group (the routes with the same rps in the scenario file) stay in the group, shared among the routes that stay in proportion to their rps in the file; the sum of rps is unchanged, so the naive estimate is the same
allocation.naive_estimate: unchanged: it scales with the sum of rps only, and the sum of rps is the same

allocation.stop_rule: the run stops (no prediction) when a group is left with no route, or when the php CPU time the model gives for one request of a route (the CPU-time mark's bound) is above half of the request timeout
